column2: Elijah's prophet title, Tishbite/Thesbon origin, Gilead and the full God-of-hosts/God-of-Israel oath retain no dew or rain except his word.
The Lord's word to Elijah introduces the next command as a separate short unit.
Eastward movement and hiding at Chorrath facing the Jordan retain direction, location and ordinary divine address to Elijah.
Drinking from the wadi and God's future command to ravens to sustain him remain distinct provisions.
Elijah acts according to the word and stays at Chorrath facing the Jordan, preserving the repeated geographical relation.
Bread in the morning and meat in the evening remain separately assigned; both foods are not supplied at both times.
After days, the wadi dries because no rain occurred, retaining the causal explanation without a stated number of days.
A new word to Elijah introduces the relocation command, without merging the two revelations.
Rise, Zarephath in Sidonian territory, behold and the already-commanded widow retain the full instruction.
City gate, behold the wood-gathering widow, Elijah's call after her and polite request for a little water in a vessel remain.
As she goes for water, the further bread-morsel request specifies in your hand, preserving the successive requests.
The living-God oath denies a hearth cake, retaining flour in a water jar, little oil, two sticks, plural children and eat-and-die expectation.
Take courage, carry out her plan, make Elijah's little cake first and prepare for herself and children afterward retain the order.
For introduces the divine promise: neither flour jar nor oil flask diminishes until the Lord gives rain, preserving both negatives and endpoint.
The woman acts, and she, he and her children eat, retaining all three subjects and no added duration.
The two undiminished provisions fulfill the Lord's word through Elijah, retaining the repeated wording.
The household mistress's son becomes severely ill until no breath remains; no additional diagnosis is supplied.
The mother's distancing question and accusation of remembered wrongs and son's death remain her speech, not a narrator's causal explanation.
Elijah requests the son, takes him from her bosom, carries him to his upper lodging and lays him on his bed.
Alas, Lord, Witness of the widow and Thou hast brought harm by killing her son preserve the selected direct lament.
column3: Witness and the declarative accusation remain despite difficulty; neither an interrogative nor a familiar Lord-my-God formula is substituted.

column2: Three breathings into the child, calling on the Lord and the request for the child's soul to return preserve selected action and prayer.
column3: Soul for psyche remains provisional between life and soul; breathing is not changed to stretching over, and no medical procedure is inferred.

column2: It happened so and the child's cry retain the short selected result, without adding an explicit Lord-heard clause.
Propose Look for Behold to render blepe as a natural imperative to the mother. Descent, return of her son and his living remain.
The woman's behold, recognition of the man of God and truth of the Lord's word in his mouth remain distinct from the prior Look command.
Many days, third year, appearance to Ahab and promised rain over the land retain the selected time and condition.
Elijah goes to appear before Ahab while severe famine is in Samaria; the two statements remain separate.
Ahab summons steward Obadiah, whose great fear of the Lord is explicitly narrated.
Jezebel's striking prophets contrasts with Obadiah hiding one hundred in groups of fifty and sustaining them with bread and water.
column3: Fifty to a cave expresses the distribution; no individual cave names or other provisions are invented.

column2: The water-spring/wadi search seeks grass to preserve horses and mules, retaining the conditional hope and livestock-loss concern.
The route is divided and both Ahab and Obadiah go alone on different ways, retaining repeated alone.
Obadiah and Elijah meet each alone; hurrying, face-fall and the recognition question retain all actions and ordinary lord address.
Elijah identifies himself and orders the report behold Elijah; is here supplies the presentative's implied location.
Obadiah's sin question and fear of being handed to Ahab for death remain his protest, not a claim that Elijah intends murder.
The oath, exhaustive search, denial of Elijah's presence and burning of kingdom and territories remain in Obadiah's report.
column3: Burned retains eneprēsen; an oath extracted from kingdoms is not substituted from another reading.

column2: The quoted command repeats go, report and behold Elijah, preserving Obadiah's emphasis.
The feared Spirit removal to an unknown land, report to Ahab, threatened death and lifelong divine fear remain.
column3: The future removal is Obadiah's feared scenario, not a narrated disappearance or promised outcome.

column2: The negative question recounts actual killing by Jezebel, one hundred hidden prophets in fifties and bread/water provision in full.
The third quoted announcement culminates in he will kill me, retaining the speaker's strong prediction.
Elijah's living-Lord-of-hosts oath assures appearance this day, preserving divine service language and timing.
Obadiah reports and Ahab runs out to meet Elijah, retaining the specific running action.
Ahab's repeated Elijah address and perverting-Israel accusation remain a question.
Elijah denies the accusation, assigns it to Ahab and father's house, and distinguishes plural abandonment from singular following the Baalim.
All Israel, 450 prophets of shame and 400 grove prophets at Jezebel's table are summoned to Carmel, preserving both groups.
Ahab sends throughout Israel and gathers all prophets at Carmel, retaining the stated breadth without claiming a separate attendance count.
Limping on both knees, the Lord/Baal alternatives and the people's silence retain the selected bodily image.
column3: Knees is not changed to opinions or branches; the figurative choice remains interpretable without replacing the source wording.

column2: Elijah's utterly-alone claim and both 450 Baal and 400 grove prophets remain.
column3: The alone claim is not harmonized with Obadiah's hidden hundred; it remains Elijah's speech in this setting.

column2: Two oxen, their choice and preparation, wood placement and both no-fire restrictions retain the proposed test's parallel actions.
Their gods plural contrast with Elijah's Lord my God; divine identity is tied to answering with fire and the whole people approve.
Prophets of shame choose and prepare first because they are many, call their god and add no fire, preserving the reason and restriction.
Morning-to-noon calling repeats Hear us twice, with no voice and no hearing, followed by running on the altar.
Elijah's mockery retains loud calling, god claim, chattering, possible business and possible sleep followed by getting up.
column3: Chattering and conducting business preserve the selected terms provisionally; relieving himself or travel is not imported.

column2: Loud cries and customary cutting with knives and lances until blood flows remain historical narration without procedural elaboration.
Prophesying past late afternoon, sacrifice time, no voice and the fuller command to move away precede their actual departure.
Elijah invites the people near, and all approach, preserving command and response.
Twelve stones correspond to Israel's tribes and the naming promise Israel will be your name remains.
column3: The him antecedent in the naming clause is understood through Israel's patriarchal reference; Elijah is not explicitly renamed by the translation.

column2: Building stones in the Lord's name, repairing the demolished altar and a surrounding trench holding two metretes of seed remain.
column3: Trench interprets thaala; the seed-volume description is retained without an invented width or modern capacity.

column2: Piling split wood, cutting the offering, laying it on the wood and repeated piling on the altar remain in sequence.
Four water jars are poured, then the action is repeated twice more with commands and responses explicitly retained.
Water runs around the altar and the trench is filled, preserving both water locations.
The full Abraham/Isaac/Israel invocation, repeated hear me, this-day fire request, people's knowledge, Thou/Thy and because of Thee remain.
column3: Because of Thee renders dia with accusative; by Thy word is not substituted from a familiar form.

column2: Repeated hear me with fire and the selected Thou hast turned their heart backward remain.
column3: Backward does not settle whether this means restoration or a prior turning away; to Thyself again is not supplied.

column2: Heavenly fire consumes offering, wood and trench water, then licks stones and dust, preserving the selected order and subjects.
All fall on faces and confess Truly the Lord is God, He is God, retaining the emphatic repetition.
Seizure, none spared, descent to Kishon and Elijah's slaughter remain with explicit agency, without expanding the narrated violence.
The command to eat and drink is grounded in the sound of rain's footsteps, preserving the unusual sound image.
Ahab goes to eat/drink while Elijah ascends Carmel, bends earthward and places his face between knees.
The attendant looks seaward and reports nothing; both the sevenfold command and sevenfold return remain.
At the seventh time, behold a footprint-shaped little cloud bringing water; the chariot command and preventive rain clause remain.
column3: Footprint retains ichnos rather than a hand, and bringing water is not changed to rising from the sea.

column2: Darkening sky, clouds, wind and great rain precede Ahab weeping and traveling to Jezreel.
column3: Wept preserves eklai en's selected lexical reading; riding is not substituted to fit the chariot context.
